extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers conducting systematic reviews / evidence synthesis (e.g., nursing and social work students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating the methodological quality and risk of bias of studies included in a systematic review, including what types of bias to consider and which tools/resources to use. Focused on selecting and applying appropriate risk-of-bias / quality-assessment approaches for included study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate studies for risk of bias with an appropriate tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies should be evaluated for risk of bias with a tool that fits the study designs included in your systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select risk-of-bias / quality-assessment tools that match the primary study designs in your review (e.g., RoB tools for randomized trials, appropriate instruments for observational or qualitative studies). See the 'Quality Assessment/Risk of Bias Tools' resources on the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological quality (critical appraisal)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Methodological quality refers to critical appraisal of a study or systematic review and the extent to which study authors conducted and reported their research to the highest possible standard." (Cochrane Handbook)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well the study was designed, conducted, analyzed, and reported — not just whether results are presented. Use critical appraisal to judge the trustworthiness of study methods and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of bias (systematic deviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bias refers to systematic deviation of results or inferences from the truth. These deviations can occur as a result of flaws in design, conduct, analysis, and/or reporting." (Cochrane Handbook)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize bias as systematic error distinct from random error; it may be introduced at many stages (design, conduct, analysis, reporting) and may not always be detectable or quantifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias can distort effect estimates (direction and magnitude uncertain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias can lead to either underestimation or overestimation of the true effect of an intervention, with varying degrees of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing studies, consider that biases may change the magnitude or even direction of reported effects; it is often difficult to predict or quantify this, so report uncertainty and consider sensitivity analyses where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias sources include investigators, review authors, research-process limitations, and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Biases may arise from the actions of primary study investigators, review authors, or limitations in the research process, and can be influenced by conflicts of interest (Boutron et al., 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider potential author-level and study-level sources of bias, and evaluate disclosed and undisclosed conflicts of interest when judging study credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider common types of bias (publication, location, citation, language, outcome reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of bias can also include: Publication bias, Location bias, Citation bias, Language bias, Outcome reporting bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting searches, selection, and synthesis, explicitly look for and assess these reporting/publication biases (e.g., by searching grey literature, checking trial registries, and comparing protocols to published reports). Consult Cochrane Handbook Chapter 7 and IOM guidance on reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer contemporary tools focusing on internal validity / risk of bias for quantitative health studies
rubrics_metrics.description: "Most recent tools for assessing the internal validity of findings from quantitative studies in health now focus on risk of bias, whereas previous tools targeted the broader notion of ‘methodological quality’." (Boutron et al., 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modern risk-of-bias instruments that emphasize internal validity for quantitative studies rather than older broad 'quality' checklists; choose instruments suited to the study design and the review question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authoritative guidance and chapter-level references when assessing bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to Cochrane Handbook Chapter 7: Considering Bias and Conflicts of Interest Among the Included Studies; Chapter 8: Assessing Risk of Bias in a Randomized Trial; and IOM (2011) 'Finding What Works in Health Care: Reporting Bias'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the methods and examples in these handbooks for structured assessment, documentation, and reporting of risk-of-bias judgments in your review; consult training resources such as Evidence Synthesis Academy modules for practical instruction.
